title: Close Update: Wall Street Loses Grip as Inflation Estimates Spook Market
text:
Close Update: Wall Street Loses Grip as Inflation Estimates Spook Market May 02, 2018, 04:28:59 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Spooked by fears of accelerating inflation with slower economic growth, Wall Street reversed gains in the wake of the statement from the Federal Open Market Committee, driving the Dow Jones Industrial Average to its lowest level in a month. Although losses for the Dow were mitigated by gains in component stock Apple ( AAPL ), the blue chip index closed lower for a fourth straight day.
Wall Street was mostly defensive for the majority of the day as investors braced for the FOMC statement and how recent signs of inflation and wage pressure would be incorporated into monetary policy. The knee-jerk reaction to the seemingly dovish statement quickly evaporated when inflation and growth projections underscored the risk of stagflation. The 10-year Treasury note backed off the 3.0% yield, but climbed back to 2.97% before the close.
On the earnings front, upbeat results from Apple helped keep the Nasdaq above water. The tech giant beat Wall Street's profit and sales expectations even as iPhone X sales were below estimates. The stock raced to a 10-day high at the open, slicing through resistance at its 50- and 100-day moving averages.
On the other end of the spectrum was Snap ( SNAP ) which missed revenue and daily-active user estimates from Wall Street analysts. The company also reported a loss of $0.17 per share, though that was narrower than the $0.20 loss last year, and was in-line with expectations.
On the economic front, a survey from Automated Data Processing showed the private sector added 204,000 new jobs in April, beating the consensus estimate of 190,000, but down from a revised 228,000 increase in March.
Thursday's generous economic calendar includes weekly jobless claims, the trade deficit, non-farm productivity and unit labor costs, factory orders and the PMI and ISM services sector indices, all of which serve as a prelude to the pivotal non-farm payroll data on Friday.
